body: Botswana cars are covered in white paint similar to neighboring southern African countries.
Botswana license plates feature white front plates and yellow rear plates, unique in southern Africa.
Signs in Botswana are usually in English with indigenous language town names.
Typical Botswana landscape is dry, flat, with arid soil, shrubs, and small trees.
Road lines outside are yellow for outer and white for center, like other Southern African countries.
Botswana has unique black-and-yellow striped signposts, not found elsewhere in Southern Africa.
Curbs and guardrails often striped black-and-yellow, red-and-white, or black-and-white.
Small red-and-white chevrons are common along roads in Botswana and South Africa.
Directional signs have green backgrounds with road numbers typical of Botswana.
Older road signs sometimes have blue backgrounds, unique to Botswana.
Houses in Botswana range from shacks to modern bungalows, including traditional round huts.
Image blurs appear randomly, mostly in urban areas, obscuring parts of panorama coverage.
Botswana has many unique regions. This image breaks down distinct landscapes by soil and vegetation.
Coverage in Botswana is limited due to sparse roads, denser in the east and near Gaborone.
Roads map showing paved and unpaved roads with simpler visualization for easy reading.
Most of Botswana is flat as a pancake. Isolated hills appear in two specific areas.
Southeastern region near Gaborone has many semi-arid hills with short shrubs.
The eastern pocket north of Francistown features red soil with arid, autumn-colored vegetation.
Middle western region has bright white sandy soil with very dry vegetation.
The A35 road is identifiable by its grainy asphalt and a power line to the west.
The A33 road features a lush landscape with tall grass and green trees to the north.
Road along southern border near Middlepits has red-tinted asphalt and arid landscape.
Gaborone, the capital, looks richer and more developed than most of Botswana.
Francistown features a lone hill with radio antennas, distinguishing it from Gaborone.
Maun is notable for its bright white sandy soil, typical for the middle western region.
A2 western part features overcast coverage, making the route recognizable.
Chobe Flood Plains has winding dirt roads, lush bushes, and wildlife such as elephants and warthogs.
A30 road features autumn feel with orange trees and tall grass along the route.
Salt pans in central-eastern Botswana show as lakes with nearby dirt roads and sparse trees.
Rural dirt tracks outside Gaborone present with orange-red dirt and green vegetation surroundings.
A33 in Sibuya Forest Reserve is under construction but some segments look normal.
Road north of Maun to Khwai has white sandy soil and tall green trees along sides.
A20 road has clean asphalt with red soil and sparse gray trees around.
Southeast A20 near Tshabong is recently repainted with bright yellow lines and dark asphalt.
Tsodilo Hills notable for large rocky protruding hills, surrounded by dirt road coverage.
Silos in Pandamatenga are distinctive and visible all around the town.
